2607.21106.title: AttriMem: Attribution-Guided Process Feedback for Agent Memory Learning
2607.21106.paper_summary: Effective memory is crucial for LLM agents, yet constructing it effectively remains challenging. A memory-construction policy decides what information to extract, store, update, compress, or discard as interactions accumulate. Heuristic memory methods rely on subjective, task-specific rules, which can misalign with downstream objectives and limit cross-task adaptability. RL-based methods, by contrast, learn from task feedback but mainly use outcome- or module-level rewards. These coarse signals indicate task success but cannot identify which intermediate memory contents support the final answer, creating a fine-grained credit-assignment bottleneck. However, constructing such process feedback is prohibitively difficult because intermediate memory decisions lack unique ground-truth targets, while the appropriate credit varies with the agent's uncertain reasoning trajectory and therefore cannot be specified in advance. We propose AttriMem, an attribution-guided process-feedback framework for learning memory-construction policies with RL. AttriMem augments the global outcome reward with local rewards derived from token-level contributions to the final answer. Experiments on long-horizon dialogue question answering show that AttriMem outperforms retrieval-based, heuristic, and RL-based baselines, generalizes across benchmarks and answer models, stabilizes RL optimization.
2607.21106.paper_summary_zh: 有效的記憶對於LLM代理至關重要，但有效構建記憶仍然具有挑戰性。記憶構建策略決定了在互動累積的過程中，應該提取、存儲、更新、壓縮或丟棄哪些信息。啟發式記憶方法依賴於主觀的、特定任務的規則，這可能與下游目標不一致，並限制跨任務的適應性。相比之下，基於強化學習的方法從任務反饋中學習，但主要使用結果或模塊級的獎勵。這些粗略的信號指示任務成功，但無法確定哪些中間記憶內容支持最終答案，從而造成細粒度的信用分配瓶頸。然而，構建這樣的過程反饋是極其困難的，因為中間記憶決策缺乏獨特的真實目標，而適當的信用則隨著代理的不確定推理軌跡而變化，因此無法提前指定。我們提出了AttriMem，一個基於歸因的過程反饋框架，用於通過強化學習學習記憶構建策略。AttriMem通過來自於對最終答案的標記級貢獻的局部獎勵來增強全局結果獎勵。在長期對話問題回答的實驗中，AttriMem的表現超過了基於檢索的、啟發式的和基於強化學習的基準，並且在基準和答案模型之間具有良好的泛化能力，穩定了強化學習的優化。
